hot_topics.topic: AI Infrastructure Faces Power Challenges Amid Expansion
hot_topics.synthesis: The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure, including new data centers, is driving significant energy demand, prompting a major US grid operator to plan power cuts to prevent blackouts. Verizon is investing heavily in dark fiber deals to connect Google data centers and converting central offices into smaller AI-supporting facilities. Meanwhile, a $100 billion data center project in Utah faces local opposition over environmental concerns and lack of public input.

hot_topics.topic: AI Writing Models Refuse Author Style Mimicry
hot_topics.synthesis: OpenAI's ChatGPT now refuses direct requests to imitate the writing styles of famous authors, instead aiming to capture broad qualities while maintaining its own distinct voice. Despite ongoing skepticism and the emergence of AI detection tools, experts predict that as AI-generated writing improves, people will increasingly accept and even appreciate it, making it harder to distinguish from human work.

hot_topics.topic: Open-Source AI Platforms Grapple with Deepfake Misuse
hot_topics.synthesis: Hugging Face, a popular open-source AI model repository, is under scrutiny for failing to prevent its image editing models from creating nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes, particularly of women and children. This issue has reignited intense debate within the AI community regarding the critical need for better alignment and control mechanisms for increasingly capable AI systems, as many open-source models lack robust ethical guardrails.

hot_topics.topic: X Launches New Financial Services Platform in the US
hot_topics.synthesis: Elon Musk's "X Money" platform is rolling out in the US, offering a digital wallet, peer-to-peer payments similar to Venmo, and a metal Visa card. This financial service is a core component of Musk's vision to transform X into an "everything app," with initial access for X Premium and Premium+ subscribers who can also benefit from boosted APY rates.

hot_topics.topic: Apple Introduces New Leasing Program for Devices
hot_topics.synthesis: Apple has officially launched its "Apple Upgrade" device leasing program in the US, in partnership with Klarna, making iPhones, Macs, iPads, and Apple Watches more accessible. This program allows users to lease devices with options to keep, pay off, or upgrade them early, addressing the rising prices of some Apple products.

hot_topics.topic: AI Policy, Open-Weight Models & Geopolitical Competition
hot_topics.synthesis: The release of open-weight AI models, such as Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 with its restrictive commercial license, is intensifying debates over AI policy and control. Anthropic's CEO, Dario Amodei, has weighed in, expressing concerns about China's growing AI capabilities while not opposing open-weight models outright. Discussions revolve around the risks and benefits of making powerful AI model weights publicly available.

hot_topics.topic: Major Earthquake Strikes Japan's Kyushu Island
hot_topics.synthesis: A powerful 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck Japan's southern main island of Kyushu, causing significant damage and injuries. Reports indicate people were trapped in a collapsed shopping mall. Authorities are assessing the full extent of the disaster.

hot_topics.topic: US Military Munitions Shortage Amid Iran Conflict
hot_topics.synthesis: The US has paused its war with Iran, facing questions about critically low munitions stockpiles after just five months of intermittent conflict. This shortage highlights a broader issue of military unpreparedness to deter or engage in a larger-scale war, such as with China. Experts suggest the crisis reveals that past war plans might have relied on unrealistic assumptions about conflict duration and resource needs.

hot_topics.topic: Trump Holds Separate High-Stakes Meetings with Zelenskyy and Netanyahu
hot_topics.synthesis: President Trump is set to hold separate high-stakes meetings with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Washington. The meetings come amidst signs of friction between Trump and Netanyahu, who both face domestic pressures, including an unpopular war for Trump and re-election challenges for Netanyahu. Discussions will likely focus on their respective regional conflicts.

items.title: The light narrows
items.summary: The author describes how his father's death led him to jiu-jitsu, followed by experiences of defeat, low testosterone, and the temptation of performance-enhancing chemicals.

items.title: 5th Circuit blocks Texas law requiring websites to filter "harmful" speech
items.summary: The 5th Circuit Court of Appeals blocked a Texas law requiring websites to filter "harmful" speech for minors, ruling that the monitoring and filtering requirement is preempted by Section 230 of the federal Communications Decency Act. Tech lobby groups successfully challenged portions of the SCOPE Act.

items.title: A missing underscore sent innocent man to prison for 18 months
items.summary: A single missing underscore in a username led to an innocent Nova Scotia man being imprisoned for 18 months during a 2018 child-luring investigation. Police mistakenly requested records for "fus_ro_dah" instead of the perpetrator's "fus__ro_dah."

items.title: As US measles cases rise, biotech firms start developing new treatments
items.summary: As US measles cases reach a 35-year high due to declining vaccination rates, biotech firms and academic groups are developing new treatments and short-term protections for infected or vulnerable individuals. However, these countermeasures are years away from availability and their acceptance by vaccine-refusers is uncertain.

items.title: ChatGPT starts blocking direct requests to copy an author's style
items.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT is now refusing direct requests to generate text in the exact style of famous authors, instead offering responses that capture broad qualities while maintaining its own distinct voice. This behavior applies to both living and deceased authors, contrasting with earlier findings.

items.title: Verizon touts $1B dark fiber deal for Google data centers as first of many
items.summary: Verizon announced a $1 billion deal to connect Google data centers using its dark fiber routes and is converting central offices into small data centers for AI inference workloads. This is part of a new "AI Connect" initiative, with Verizon anticipating additional multi-billion dollar AI-related deals.

items.title: “Google and Reddit do not own the Internet," web scraper says after court win
items.summary: Google lost a court case against web scraper SerpApi but intends to continue its fight to block AI bots from scraping its search results, citing copyright protection and potential disruption to relationships with rights holders. SerpApi was accused of circumventing anti-scraping technology and selling scraped content.

items.summary: Families in Seattle paid tribute to the three victims killed in a shooting at a food festival, expressing their grief.

items.summary: The family of a victim criticized Bryan Kohberger, accused of killing four Idaho students, for challenging his murder conviction after initially entering a plea to avoid the death penalty.

items.summary: Firefighters in France's Gironde region are preparing for a sharp rise in temperatures, which is expected to complicate efforts to contain ongoing wildfires.

items.summary: The 2026 Booker Prize longlist features 13 books, including new works from established authors like Douglas Stuart, Marlon James, and Elizabeth Strout, alongside several debut authors.

The guide also reveals that ChatGPT Work on mobile can access the internet, unlike its Code Interpreter container.

items.title: A great idea that everyone hates
items.summary: Charging household electricity users spot prices, while politically unpopular, is proposed as a straightforward solution to meaningfully impact electricity prices and incentivize new investment. This contrasts with current annualized average pricing which masks real-time fluctuations and higher overall costs.

items.title: The midterms, 100 days out
items.summary: With fewer than 100 days until Election Day, both Democratic and Republican parties face challenges, including a cash-poor DNC and an unmotivated GOP base, as they navigate primary season and work to keep candidates on course.

items.title: Antares raises $470M to build nuclear reactors for the US military
items.summary: Antares has raised $470 million to develop small modular nuclear reactors, ranging from 100 kW to 1 MW, specifically for deployment at U.S. Air Force bases. This funding aims to provide advanced energy solutions for military infrastructure.

items.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei responds: doesn’t oppose open-weight models, but fears Chinese AI
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has clarified his stance on open-weight AI models, stating he doesn't oppose them but expresses concerns about China's growing AI capabilities. This reflects ongoing debates about AI development and international competition.

items.title: Apple launches ‘Upgrade’ device leasing program in partnership with Klarna
items.summary: Apple has launched its "Upgrade" device leasing program in the US, in partnership with Klarna, offering monthly prices for iPhones, Apple Watches, Macs, and iPads. This initiative aims to make Apple devices more accessible to consumers.

items.summary: Apple is facing a lawsuit from three users who lost over $1.8 million to a fraudulent crypto wallet app downloaded from the App Store, challenging Apple's claims about its app review process ensuring user safety.

items.title: As rivals chase acquisitions, Peacock bets on bundles through a new deal with YouTube
items.summary: Peacock is focusing on content bundles, signing a new deal with YouTube to integrate its content into the YouTube experience, allowing viewers to discover and watch Peacock content directly within the platform.

items.title: Data centers may face temporary power cuts to prevent blackouts on largest US grid
items.summary: The largest US grid operator plans to implement temporary power cuts to large data centers starting next year to prevent blackouts. This measure addresses increasing energy demands from data centers, particularly those supporting AI workloads.

items.title: Elon Musk’s X Money app is rolling out in the U.S.
items.summary: Elon Musk's X Money app, a payment platform, is rolling out in the U.S. and is currently available to X Premium and Premium+ subscribers. This expands X's features as Musk aims to transform it into an "everything app."

items.title: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises
items.summary: Fish Audio has raised a $52 million seed round to develop AI voice models for creators and enterprises, having already gained over 8 million users and generating $21 million in annual recurring revenue since its launch last year.

items.title: Granola launches an Apple Watch app
items.summary: Granola has launched an Apple Watch app designed for in-person notetaking, expanding its utility for users seeking convenience and quick information capture.

items.title: Lyft and Baidu enter London’s robotaxi battleground as testing begins
items.summary: Lyft and Baidu are introducing their robotaxi services to London, with Baidu's Apollo Go autonomous vehicles becoming available through the Freenow mobility network, which Lyft acquired in 2025. This marks an expansion of autonomous vehicle testing into a major European city.

items.title: OpenAI’s Hugging Face breach has reignited the debate over alignment and control
items.summary: An "OpenAI's Hugging Face breach" has intensified the debate over AI alignment and control, raising questions about whether increasingly capable AI systems need better alignment, containment, or both.

items.summary: Recursive Superintelligence has signed a $410 million compute deal with Amazon, which represents the majority of the company's total fundraising to date. This substantial agreement highlights the high demand for computing resources in advanced AI development.

items.title: Satya Nadella says companies that trust one AI for everything may not survive
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella cautions that companies relying solely on one AI model for everything may not survive, emphasizing the importance of having proprietary models or AI gateways to separate prompts from the core model.

items.title: Thea Energy lands $20M federal grant to build its magnets for fusion reactors
items.summary: Fusion power startup Thea Energy received a $20 million federal grant from ARPA-E to scale the production of its high-temperature superconducting magnets, essential components for fusion reactors.

items.title: WhatsApp now lets you make calls using its web app
items.summary: WhatsApp has enabled calling features, including screen-sharing and reactions, on its web application, bringing its functionality closer to its smartphone and desktop apps.

items.title: A Peace Plan for the Data Center Wars
items.summary: A proposed $100 billion data center project in Box Elder County, Utah, is facing opposition despite its remote location, use of recycled water, and tax contributions, primarily due to concerns about environmental impact and lack of public consultation. The project highlights growing conflicts over data center development.

items.title: America’s Munitions Mess Is Even Worse Than You Think

This crisis suggests that prior war plans were based on unrealistic assumptions about the length and intensity of engagements.

He highlights the repetitive nature of these events and the perpetrator's history of radicalization.

items.title: Tyler Cowen: You’ll Learn to Love AI Writing
items.summary: Tyler Cowen predicts that people will learn to appreciate AI-generated writing as it improves, despite current skepticism and tools like Substack's Scan for AI. He anticipates AI writing will become more indistinguishable from human writing and overcome its current clichés.

items.summary: The author finds smart rings appealing as AI gadgets, noting the significant improvements in dictation technology that allow for efficient speech-to-text for emails and messages. While current AI dictation has minor quirks, its usefulness for quick communication is highlighted.
